I'm currently working on an initial versin of iris/program_logic/weakestpre.v, and I'm running into issues proving that wp_pre is contractive. The Rocq proof makes heavy use of f_contractive and f_equiv to make progress, and I find myself looking for different instances of OFE.Contractive to try to emulate these tactics, without much progress.

Any recommendations?
For now, there's similar code in #iris-lean > Iris-Lean demos, which gives me the name of some of the instances that I need.
Hmm, maybe it would be useful to have a loogle instance with iris-lean loaded...
Yeah searching is a problem but fortunately f_contractive and f_equiv aren't that clever. Here is another example for your perusal.
Maybe taking fun_prop from Mathlib would also not be a bad idea

Fernando LEAL said:

Hmm, maybe it would be useful to have a loogle instance with iris-lean loaded...

You can use loogle locally. See the README of the repository
Yeap, since then I did manage to have work locally, and it has been working like a charm
Maybe it's about time I set it up myself instead of guessing and checking with rg :sweat_smile:
You just gotta edit the lakefile.lean (to add Iris and pin Mathlib to Iris's Lean version) and edit the server.py so it calls loogle with --module Iris
I didn't find these instructions in the Readme
Fwiw you also have https://github.com/leanprover-community/LeanSearchClient
You can make search queries to multiple search engines from inside lean files, including inside proof blocks.
Afaik it is a dependency of mathlib, so you can use it in math projects without extra steps. For iris, I am guessing some initial setup is required.

Fernando LEAL said:

You just gotta edit the lakefile.lean (to add Iris and pin Mathlib to Iris's Lean version) and edit the server.py so it calls loogle with --module Iris

That sounds super cool! I wanted to have something like this but struggled to setup loogle. Could you share your setup somehow? I am also wondering if we can integrate the setup into the repository. Maybe we can have an IrisLoogle subproject which has the right dependencies and where one has a scratch file that imports Iris that one can use for searches?

I have uploaded the changes I made to the mainstream repo here:
https://github.com/ayhon/iris-loogle

After cloning, if you have nix, it should be as simple as running nix develop and python server.py to have it working in local host
why the toolchain downgrade?
afaik Iris is currently in v4.29.0, so we need to downgrade Mathlib so they can be both in the same project
We could technically drop Mathlib, but I think it's nice it's included anyways because it may be useful to know that I can simply copy-paste a definition from there

When I run ./server.py from @Fernando LEAL 's repo, I keep getting uncaught exception: import Iris.Instances.UPred.Instance failed, environment already contains 'Iris.UPred.mk.congr_simp' from Iris.Algebra.UPred. Any clue why?

Maybe related, the lakefile.lean that I shared assumes that you have iris-lean cloned under that name in the parent folder, and uses that as it's source. That might also be where you have your local changes
See #general > loogle for local use @ 💬 for how to use loogle for local use. The instructions worked great for me and I was able to get a local loogle server running for Iris Lean without problems!
Ralf remaked today that it would be great to have the loogle instructions to the repo README.
